note: M1b noise list (RIG.md section 12.6, ruling 2026-11-17). Hand-written from the m1b-freeze captures of 2026-11-17 and (the Defender signature / AppX rules) the m1b-gate4 runs of 2026-11-18 (ruling 2026-11-18: Defender noise, proper fix and full rerun); mk_labels.py does not generate it. vm/truth/m1b.sh passes it as an extra --labels file to every M1b truth (collect and freeze) and hashes it into each run's label digest. Windows-owned areas whose state changes on Windows' own schedule or belongs to a Windows store: every rule is ambient and anchored under a Windows-owned root (checked by the selftest, which also checks that no rule matches a leftover, user_data or kept_owner item of any frozen truth). Churn is never labelled leftover: what this list misses and only one freeze run shows is excluded from the frozen truth by the freeze rule.

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: Windows Push Notification Services (WNS) channel backup of an inbox Windows component (MicrosoftWindows.*_cw5n1h2txyewy, e.g. the IRIS client): channel ids, creation and expiry times renewed on the service's schedule. Windows' own channels only: an app's channel (Notepad++ in the M0 truth) stays the app's.

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: IRIS (Windows content delivery: Spotlight, tips) state per user: action creatives, timers, WNS channel status refreshed on its own schedule.

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: Activity state (HAM) of inbox Windows components (MicrosoftWindows.*_cw5n1h2txyewy: Spotlight, IRIS, Windows Backup) per user. Windows' own packages only.

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: Windows rules-engine background report stamps per user (ReportStateTimestamp).

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: Windows Spotlight desktop state per user (IRIS content timers).

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: Explorer's discardable COM component-category cache per user, rebuilt by the shell.

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: Taskbar state stamp the shell rewrites at every refresh.

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: Font cache service (LocalService profile) configuration expiry, renewed on its own schedule.

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: BitLocker telemetry check stamps (AADBackupCheckTimestamp), written by the BitLocker service on its schedule.

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: Registry hive defragmentation counter of the configuration manager (kernel).

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: Windows Security Center provider state (Defender AV state flags), updated by Defender.

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: Connected User Experiences and Telemetry (DiagTrack) downloaded settings and their .bk copies.

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: Windows Installer's list of temp packages it deletes itself after a transaction (the .msi files it names are relabelled by m1b.sh temp_packages).

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: Windows Update service-locator (SLS) cache, e.g. of the Microsoft Update service an MSI opts the machine into; Windows Update state.

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: System Restore initialisation flag msiexec sets at its first restore-point check (the SystemRestore key itself is ambient in the app label files); Windows state.

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: MUI resource-string cache generation key with a hex name (1a); _os.json covers the decimal ones only. Not the shell MuiCache of exe names (Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\MuiCache).

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: .NET servicing breadcrumb store (one empty file per runtime package a .NET app loaded, read by Microsoft Update to service .NET); a Windows-owned store under ProgramData\Microsoft (deny fs.programdata.microsoft), never a cleaner target.

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: Microsoft Defender signature store: each signature / engine update unpacks into a new Definition Updates\{guid} folder (gate4 2026-11-18: an update ~20 s after snap 0 in 4 of 8 rig-base runs; ruling 2026-11-18, RIG.md section 12.7). Defender-owned, never an app's.

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: Microsoft Defender engine scan cache (mpcache-<hash>.bin, its .NN parts and .manifest), rebuilt by a signature / engine update (ruling 2026-11-18).

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: Microsoft Defender real-time (dynamic) signature store: RtSigs\Data\<sha1> blobs Defender fetches and expires on its own schedule (the M0 null runs already showed them; ruling 2026-11-18).

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: Microsoft Defender signature-update stub (MpSigStub.exe) run state, e.g. LastStartTime, written at every signature update (ruling 2026-11-18).

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: Windows Update targeting record of the installed Defender signature package (DefenderSignature.<arch>|Version), bumped by every signature update (ruling 2026-11-18).

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: Event-log publisher Microsoft-Antimalware-Engine (this exact GUID only), re-registered by a Defender engine update (ruling 2026-11-18). Other publishers stay their app's (PowerShell's {f90714a8-...} is a leftover).

rules.label: ambient
rules.why: AppX deployment service volume flags (PackageVolumes\<n>\MutablePackagesOnline, UserMutablePackagesOnline), recreated when the service brings the volume's mutable package stores online, e.g. during a Defender platform / signature update; the M0 null runs already showed them (ruling 2026-11-18). Windows' own, never a desktop app's.
